newsitem.title: SWEDEN: KLM Cargo says geared to fight integrators - report.
newsitem.headline: KLM Cargo says geared to fight integrators - report.

text.p: KLM Cargo says it will fight integrators in Northern European markets through better cooperation with freight forwarders and shorter lead times from the region.

Michael Steen, regional sales manager for KLM Cargo in the Nordic region, the Baltic countries and northwestern Russia, told Swedish industry magazine Transport Idag that integrators could claw away more market share if nothing was done.
"Cooperation must strengthen between forwarders and airlines," Steen told the magazine.
He said Swedish shippers were choosing integrators even for large shipments.
"I know major customers in Sweden who have decided that integrators should handle all of their shipments up to 400 kg. This is quite a strong warning signal for all freight forwarders."
"Something must be done. The threat is way too serious not to be taken seriously."
KLM Cargo, which recently launched a service with a Shorts Belfast with a 30 tonne capacity from Stockholm daily Monday to Friday, said this cut lead times for Finnish customers.
He told the magazine the Shorts Belfast could handle pallets that could be built to fit directly into a Boeing 747 Combi version or a Boeing 747 freighter, shortening reloading times at Schiphol.

"We have stopped our Finland freighter, an Electra from Helsinki once a week. Instead we can ship goods by ferry every night from (Finnish city) Abo to Stockholm and put them on the Shorts Belfast to transport them further," Steen said.
"We have halved our lead times for Finnish goods, from four days to two," he said.
KLM also flies a Lockheed Electra with a 15 tonne capacity from southern Swedish city Malmo daily Tuesday through Sunday.
